content: The Quality Assurance Review Center (QARC) is a publicly funded, non-profit healthcare organization based in Providence, Rhode Island. Its primary role is to provide quality assurance for radiotherapy and manage diagnostic imaging data for all National Cancer Institute (NCI)-sponsored cooperative groups. Additionally, QARC collaborates with the pharmaceutical industry to offer its services in clinical trials for anti-cancer drugs. The center receives radiotherapy data from approximately one thousand hospitals across the United States and internationally. Since its establishment in 1977, QARC has reviewed over thirty thousand cases. Furthermore, QARC maintains a strategic affiliation with the University of Massachusetts Medical School in Worcester, Massachusetts. QARC is organized into three distinct sectors: the Physics/Dosimetry Department, the Data Management Division, and the Operations Department. The Physics/Dosimetry Department is responsible for evaluating radiation dose calculations submitted for each patient under specific protocols. This department works closely with public oncology groups and private pharmaceutical companies to develop and implement new benchmarks in radiation therapy. As part of its quality assurance responsibilities, the department participates in initial, interventional, and final reviews to ensure strict adherence to protocol guidelines and maintain the highest level of integrity. The Data Management Division handles and processes all forms of patient-related data for any given protocol. This data typically includes diagnostic imaging, physics benchmarks, and radiology reports. The diagnostic imaging data often involves Computed Tomography (CT), Positron Emission Tomography (PET), and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans. Occasionally, Gallium and Bone scans are also obtained if required by a protocol. With the increasing use of nuclear medicine in radiology, QARC aims to build and maintain an extensive database through its Data Management Division. The Operations Department focuses on establishing and maintaining collaborative relationships between QARC and various NCI-supported oncology groups, as well as the pharmaceutical industry. It also works with its University of Massachusetts Medical School affiliate on matters related to accounting and employment. QARC has had pharmaceutical contracts for clinical trials with companies such as Sanofi-Aventis, Amgen, and GlaxoSmithKline. NCI oncology groups, including ACOSOG, COG, ECOG, SWOG, and CALGB, require that radiotherapy materials for their protocols be submitted to QARC for review.
